agents.name: Rex
agents.note: SPRINT 64 (V0.29.18) COMPLETE -- 1/1 (US-492 obdctl). Built the on-Pi operator CLI: `obdctl [status|start|stop|restart|kill] [<unit>|all]`, deploy-installed to /usr/local/bin. THE DECISION THAT SHAPED EVERYTHING: implemented in PYTHON, not bash. AC-10 allows either, but AC-2 demands ONE unit list -- and the only way to have literally one is for both consumers to IMPORT it. A bash tool would have had to parse a manifest or mirror it, i.e. the second list the AC forbids. New src/pi/ops/unit_manifest.py is that SSOT; src/pi/splash/service_control.py's US-403 SERVICE_ALLOWLIST is now DERIVED from it. THE SUBTLETY WORTH CARRYING: the kiosk list had to stay NARROW (4 units, mirrored by the 51- polkit rule) while the manifest holds 8 -- so each entry carries `kioskVerbs` DEFAULTING TO EMPTY. The narrowness is then a property of the data model, not of anyone's discipline: adding a unit to the manifest cannot widen the kiosk's reach. MOST IMPORTANT LESSON, and it is the same shape as last sprint's CSS finding: my first derivation test was `assert SERVICE_ALLOWLIST == kioskAllowlist()` and it went GREEN against the UNREFACTORED module. Equality proves the values match TODAY, never that one COMES FROM the other -- a copy-paste satisfies it forever. Rewrote it to PERTURB the manifest and reload the consumer, watched it go RED (KeyError), then refactored. If you are testing a wiring, perturb the source; if you test the value you are testing a coincidence. SECOND FINDING, caught only by RUNNING the tool (on this Windows host, no systemctl): every unit read `unknown` and my guard banner shouted 'SAFE-SHUTDOWN GUARD IS DOWN'. `unknown` means the READ failed, not that the guard is down -- a confident wrong claim about the one unit whose status matters most, and an operator who chases a phantom outage once stops believing the banner the time it is real. Now `unknown` prints a distinct 'not confirmed down, not confirmed up'. Ran the thing; the unit tests all passed and still missed it. THIRD: the deploy step writes its wrapper via a heredoc nested in a double-quoted string sent over SSH -- static greps cannot see a mis-escaped `$@`, and that bug only surfaces on the Pi as `obdctl: not found`. tests/deploy/obdctl_wrapper_sim.sh EXECUTES the real step body off-Pi with `remote`+`sudo` stubbed, runs the wrapper it produced, and re-runs for idempotence. Wrapper points at SYSTEM python3, NOT the venv -- obdctl is what you reach for when the Pi is broken and the venv is one of the things that can be broken (two tests pin it). conditionalOutcome 2 discharged EMPIRICALLY: eclipse-sync stays in the manifest flagged installedByDeploy=False (preserving US-403+polkit byte-for-byte) and a test greps all THREE installers (deploy-pi.sh + the splash and dashboard kit install.sh -- the unit list was spread across those three files, which is WHY the SSOT was needed) to confirm none installs it, plus the converse for all 8 canonical units. Bidirectional on purpose: a one-way check lets the manifest rot on the side nobody asserts. JUDGEMENT CALLS (all in completionNotes): declined confirm => exit 2 (a script must not read a partial teardown as complete) while a not-installed unit inside `all` stays exit 0; declining during `stop all` stops everything EXCEPT the guard rather than aborting the batch, and ALL confirms are collected BEFORE the first unit is touched so a decline never strands a half-torn-down stack; `kill` always confirms (--yes to script) and is NEVER reached from a failed `stop`. Ordering is grounded in the units' own After=/Wants= lines, and STOP_ORDER is simply START_ORDER reversed -- one ordering to keep correct. GREEN: 109 targeted (63 new ops + 17 new deploy + 23 pre-existing US-403 + 6 states-http), ruff clean, bash -n clean. HOST GAPS unchanged: `make` not on PATH (ran its underlying ruff), black + mypy + shellcheck not installed. ON-PI GATE OWED: all 5 validationCriteria are ON-PI-CLI-EXERCISE and NONE can be discharged from a dev box -- exercise status/restart/stop all/kill/stop-powerwatch after deploy, and specifically check whether splash-boot/splash-grace/rfcomm-bind really do rest `inactive` (the manifest's inactiveIsNormal annotation is a claim about runtime only the Pi can confirm) and that sudo does not re-prompt mid-`stop all`. Carried debt unchanged: TD-067 (--destructive token) + TD-068 (node-probe locale codepage).
